subject: octopus
reasoning:

Since I'm not fully certain of the exact SDK signatures for chains, sweeps, and parts, I'm making reasonable guesses -- using something like a chain helper per arm with parent/role/count options, then sweeping each chain with a radius function to taper the tentacles, accepting the risk that some parameter names may not match exactly.

For the suckers, rather than using a sweep API I'll just compute my own tentacle curve points directly and place small pale spheres along the underside at each one, letting them inherit the nearest bone for binding -- simpler than trying to use a callback-based path system. I'm now working out the parametric formula for each arm's direction, radius growth, and vertical droop as a function of position along its length.

Working through the height and tube-radius functions so the arms taper naturally and the lowest, thickest sections actually rest on the floor instead of floating.

Now I'm placing the suckers along each arm, nestling small pale spheres toward the underside near the floor-facing side, and sketching the orange-red body coloring.

I'm setting up the joint hierarchy next — body as root with head and mantle as children, arms branching off root, each chain segmented into joints so the SDK can name them automatically.
